newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen stable, JGBs end higher.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen stable, JGBs end higher.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were stable in late Thursday trade after a spate of morning selling, underpinned by buying on dips, dealers said.
"There were some late buying on dips on nagging concerns over Japan's banking sector and economy. That helped push Euroyen up two ticks in the afternoon," said a Japanese dealer.
After trading to a low of 99.23 in the morning, December Euroyen rebounded to trade unchanged from its previous IMM close at 99.25 on late Thursday. Volume was at 6,655 lots.
Euroyen mirrored movements on the Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures, dealers said.
March JGB ended a shade off its high of 126.45, at 126.39 on a turnover of 350 lots.
"There were some short-covering (in the afternoon) after the morning sell-off to a low of 125.96 following Yamazaki's comments," the dealer said.
Taku Yamazaki, policy chief of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party, commented on using public funds to protect investors against debenture defaults.
The remark triggered some diversion of funds away from the bond market into the stock market, dealers said.
Dealers said the German Central Bank's concerns on the strength of the dollar had resulted in volatility in the currency market but made little impact on the Japanese yield curves.
Eurodollar futures were stable with focus on the U.S. Producer Price Index for January, due to be released on Friday, dealers said.
The September contract ended unchanged against its previous IMM close at 94.22.
